Plane electromagnetic wave calculator: wavelength, wave number, magnetic field and its direction, expression of E(r, t) and B(r, t) in any direction, circular and elliptical polarization, the wave from its expression, standing wave and reflection at normal incidence, impedance, intensity, radiation pressure, point source and penetration depth in conductors, with the wave in 3D and step by step.
¿Cómo se relacionan la longitud de onda,: How are wavelength, frequency and wave number related?
c = λ·f, k = 2π/λ y ω = 2πf. En el vacío: c = λ·f, k = 2π/λ and ω = 2πf. In vacuum, a 100 MHz wave has λ = 3·10⁸ / 10⁸ = 3 m and k = 2π/3 ≈ 2.09 rad/m.
¿Cómo se calculan el campo B, la intensi: How are the B field, the intensity and the radiation pressure calculated?
En una onda plana, B₀ = E₀/c, la intensi: In a plane wave, B₀ = E₀/c, the intensity is I = ½ε₀cE₀² and the radiation pressure on an absorbing surface is I/c. With E₀ = 100 V/m: B₀ ≈ 3.3·10⁻⁷ T and I ≈ 13.3 W/m².
A partir de la frecuencia, la longitud d: From the frequency, the wavelength or the wave number, calculate λ, k, ω, the B field and its direction, the expressions of E(r, t) and B(r, t), the intensity and the radiation pressure, in vacuum or in a material, in any direction and with linear, circular or elliptical polarization. It also reads the wave from its expression E(r, t) or B(r, t), forms the standing wave against a conductor or the reflection at another medium, and calculates the intensity of a point source and the attenuation and penetration depth in a conductor, with the wave drawn in 3D.
Onda electromagnética con los campos E y: Electromagnetic wave with the E and B fields
Lejos de la fuente, una onda electromagn: Far from the source, a harmonic electromagnetic wave travelling in the direction k̂ has the fields
$E(r, t) = E_0 cos(k·r − ωt) Ê$, &ensp;: $E(r, t) = E_0 cos(k·r − ωt) Ê$,   $B(r, t) = B_0 cos(k·r − ωt) B̂$
E, B y k̂ son perpendiculares entre sí y: E, B and k̂ are perpendicular to each other and form a right-handed triad: $B̂ = k̂ × Ê$. The two fields are in phase and their amplitudes satisfy $E_0 = v B_0$. The wave number is $k = {2π}/λ = ω/v$ and the speed $v = 1/√(μ ε)$: in vacuum $c = 1/√(μ_0 ε_0) ≈ 3·10^8$ m/s and in a material $v = c/n$, with $n = √(ε_r μ_r)$.
Si E tiene dos componentes perpendicular: If E has two perpendicular components that are out of phase, $E = E_{01} cos(k·r − ωt) ê_1 + E_{02} cos(k·r − ωt + δ) ê_2$, the tip of E describes an ellipse at each point: this is elliptical polarization. With $E_{01} = E_{02}$ and $δ = ±90°$ it is a circle (circular polarization) and |E| does not change; with δ = 0° or 180° it is linear again. The intensity is the sum of those of the two components, $I = {E_{01}^2 + E_{02}^2}/{2η}$.
Leer una onda desde su expresión: Reading a wave from its expression
En $E_0 cos(k·r − ωt + φ)$ los coeficien: In $E_0 cos(k·r − ωt + φ)$ the coefficients of x, y, z are the components of the wave vector k, and that of t is −ω. If the phase has $+ωt$, the wave travels towards $−k$. The speed is $v = ω/k$: if it comes out as c it goes through vacuum, and if it is smaller, through a medium of index $n = c/v$. With B as data, $E_0 = v B_0$ and $Ê = B̂ × k̂$.
La energía viaja con el vector de Poynti: Energy travels with the Poynting vector $S = {E × B}/μ$. Its mean value is the intensity, which depends on the impedance of the medium $η = √(μ/ε)$ (376.7 Ω in vacuum):
Una onda también lleva cantidad de movim: A wave also carries momentum: on a surface that absorbs it, it exerts a pressure $p = I/v$, and twice that if it reflects it. A point source of power P spreads the energy over spheres, so $I = P/{4π r^2}$.
Un polarizador ideal solo deja pasar la: An ideal polarizer lets through only the component of E parallel to its axis. If linearly polarized light arrives at an angle θ to the axis, $E = E_0 cos θ$ and, since the intensity is proportional to $E^2$, the output is $I = I_0 cos^2 θ$ (Malus's law). Natural light, with all directions equal, loses half at the first polarizer: $I = I_0/2$. Two crossed polarizers (at 90°) let nothing through, but an intermediate one at 45° lets through $I_0/8$ of natural light.
El vector de Poynting y el balance de en: The Poynting vector and the energy balance
El teorema de Poynting dice que la poten: Poynting's theorem says that the power leaving a volume is the flux of $S = {E × B}/μ_0$ through its surface, and that it is shared between the increase of the field energy and the heat dissipated. In a wire carrying current, E runs along the wire, B surrounds it and S enters through the surface: $S·2π a L = I^2 R$. In a capacitor being charged, the displacement current creates B at the edge and S enters through the sides: its flux is $dU/dt = V I$. In a coaxial cable the power $P = V I$ travels through the dielectric between the conductors.
Incidencia normal: reflexión y onda esta: Normal incidence: reflection and standing wave
Cuando una onda llega perpendicular a la: When a wave arrives perpendicular to the boundary with another medium, a fraction $r = {η_2 − η_1}/{η_2 + η_1}$ of the amplitude is reflected and $t = 1 + r$ is transmitted; of the energy, $R = r^2$ is reflected and $T = 1 − R$ passes. A perfect conductor reflects everything with $r = −1$, and the sum of the incoming and reflected waves is a standing wave, $E = 2E_0 sin(kz) sin(ωt)$, with nodes of E every λ/2 that do not move.
Los electrones libres de un plasma respo: The free electrons of a plasma respond to the field with a current that changes the dispersion relation: $ω^2 = ω_p^2 + c^2 k^2$, with the plasma frequency $ω_p = √({n_e e^2}/{ε_0 m_e})$ (numerically $f_p ≈ 8{.}98 √{n_e}$ Hz with $n_e$ in m<sup>-3</sup>). It is equivalent to an index $n = √(1 − ω_p^2/ω^2)$, less than 1: below $ω_p$ the wave is evanescent and is reflected; above it, it propagates with phase velocity $v_f = c/n > c$ and group velocity $v_g = c n < c$, so that $v_f v_g = c^2$. In the ionosphere, with incidence at an angle θ, the wave returns to Earth if $f ≤ f_p/cos θ$ (secant law).
Como las ecuaciones de Maxwell son linea: Since Maxwell's equations are linear, the fields add. With two similar frequencies, beats appear: $E = 2A cos(π Δf t) cos(2π f̄ t)$, an oscillation at the mean frequency with an envelope that pulses at $|f_1 − f_2|$. Two equal waves in opposite directions form a standing wave with nodes every λ/2; if the reflected one is smaller, non-zero nodes remain and the voltage standing wave ratio is $VSWR = {A_1 + A_2}/{|A_1 − A_2|}$. Two perpendicular waves with phase difference δ combine into an ellipse (linear if δ = 0° or 180°, circular if the amplitudes are equal and δ = ±90°).
Una lámina de retardo retrasa la compone: A retarder plate delays the component of E along its slow axis relative to that along the fast axis: λ/4 introduces 90° and λ/2 introduces 180°. A λ/4 at 45° to linear light makes it circular; a λ/2 at an angle θ to the linear light rotates it by 2θ. In Jones calculus the light is a complex vector $(E_x, E_y)$ and each element a 2×2 matrix, so the setup is a product of matrices.
En un medio con conductividad σ la onda: In a medium with conductivity σ the wave is attenuated: $E = E_0 e^{−αz} cos(βz − ωt)$. What decides the behaviour is the loss tangent $σ/{ωε}$. If it is much greater than 1 the medium is a good conductor, $α ≈ β ≈ √(π f μ σ)$, and the wave only enters a penetration depth $δ = 1/α$ (skin effect): in copper at 1 MHz it is about 66 μm. If it is much less than 1 it is a good dielectric and there are hardly any losses.
